exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

I usually buy Good Culture, but it is unavailable. What should I buy instead, and why?
reviewed_answer:
Buy Daisy 2% Low-Fat Cottage Cheese as your closest everyday substitute. It has a creamy, well-formed curd texture and a very short ingredient list—skim milk, cultured cream, and salt—without the gums and starches found in many competitors.

Best pick: Daisy 2% Low-Fat

Good Culture’s appeal is its thick, creamy texture, mild tang from live cultures, simple ingredients, and high protein with no added sugar. Daisy best matches that “eat it plain or with fruit” experience, though it is not fermented with live active cultures in the same way.

Choose: Daisy 2% Low-Fat Cottage Cheese, small curd.

Why: Blind taste testing rated Daisy best overall for its soft, distinct curds and rich creaminess; it also had the shortest ingredient list among brands tested.

Nutrition fit: CSPI specifically recommends Daisy 2% Low-Fat as an alternative when Good Culture is unavailable.

If you want closer to Good Culture’s style
Priority	Buy	Why
Simple ingredients + organic	Nancy’s Organic Cottage Cheese	Chefs recommend it as the closest match to Good Culture’s minimal-ingredient approach. 

Creamy, blendable texture	365 Organic Cottage Cheese	Its small, soft curds nearly melt, making it ideal for smoothies, pasta sauces, egg bites, and dips. 

Snacking and bowls	Organic Valley Cottage Cheese	It has firm, slightly bouncy curds and balanced creaminess, making it a strong runner-up for eating straight from the container. 

Cooking, lasagna, gnocchi	Breakstone’s Cottage Cheese	Smaller curds and a less watery texture work well when you need cottage cheese to hold structure in a recipe. 
What to check on the label

To replicate what you like about Good Culture, look for:

2% milkfat / low-fat rather than fat-free, for a richer mouthfeel.

Small curd, unless you prefer large curd.

High protein: Good Culture’s 2% classic provides 14 g protein per half-cup serving.

Short ingredient list: milk, cream, salt, and ideally live active cultures; avoid excessive guar gum, tapioca starch, or locust bean gum if texture matters to you.

Lower sodium if that is a concern; cottage cheese can be salty—Good Culture itself has 340 mg sodium per serving.

Bottom line: Get Daisy 2% Low-Fat first. If your store carries Nancy’s Organic, choose that instead if simple, cultured ingredients matter most; choose 365 Organic if you mainly use cottage cheese in blended or cooked dishes.
